Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 93, verses 1–2:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Tafsir of Surat al-Duha

It is Meccan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the morning brightness﴾. He swears by the entire day. It is also said: by the time of forenoon (al-duhwa), which is the time when the sun rises high.

Mujahid said: "Saja" means it became level (istawa). Ikrima said: the creation became still in it. It is also said: its darkness became settled.

Al-Asma'i said: the saj'u of the night is the covering of the day. It is said: "laylun daj" (a dark night), "bahrun saj" (a still sea), and "sama'un dhat abraj" (a sky with constellations). The rajiz (rajaz poet) said:

(Oh how lovely is the moonlit night, and the dark night (al-dajj)
and a road like the weaver's cloth (mala' al-nassaj).)

And another said:

(What is our fault, if the sea of the son of your paternal uncle has surged,
and your sea is still (saj), which does not conceal the sand-hills (al-dda'ami)?)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 93, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you.﴾ The people of tafsir (ahl al-tafsir) said: Jibril was delayed in coming to the Messenger once, so the Quraysh said: "His Lord has forsaken him and detested him."

It is also narrated that a woman said to him: "O Muhammad, I think your devil has abandoned you." So Allah the Exalted revealed this surah, and swore by what we have mentioned that He had not forsaken him nor detested him.

Zuhayr narrated from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Jundub al-Bajali, who said: "I was with the Prophet on a military expedition, and his finger was bleeding, so the Prophet said:

﴿Are you but a finger that bleeds, and in the way of Allah you have suffered what you have suffered?﴾

He said: Then Jibril was delayed, and the polytheists said: "Muhammad has been forsaken." So Allah the Exalted revealed His saying ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you.﴾" He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This hadith was related to us by Abu Muhammad al-Makki ibn Abd al-Razzaq al-Kushmayhani, who said: my grandfather Abu al-Haytham al-Firabri related to us, who said: al-Bukhari related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, from Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya ibn Hudayj, the hadith.

Some of them mentioned that the verse was revealed when the Jews asked the Messenger of Allah about the story of the People of the Cave, and about Dhu al-Qarnayn, and about the Spirit (al-Ruh). He said: "I will inform you tomorrow," and he did not say "if Allah wills." So Jibril, peace be upon him, was delayed seventeen days, and it was said: less or more. The polytheists said: "His Lord has forsaken him and detested him." So Allah the Exalted revealed this surah.

It has been read in the irregular (shadhdh) reading with the lightened form (lā waddaʿaka, with tashdid removed), whereas the well-known reading is with the doubled letter (waddaʿaka), meaning: "He has not cut off the revelation from you." (It was also said) it means: "He has not turned away from you."

With the lightened reading, its meaning is: "He has not left you." The Arabs say: "Leave (daʿ) this, abandon (dhar) this, and forsake (utruk) this," with one meaning.

As for His saying ﴿nor has He detested you﴾, meaning: He has not hated you (mā qalāka), i.e. He has not hated you. (It was also said) He has not forsaken you since you were before, and He has not hated you since He loved you.

al-Akhtal said:

(Those who guide, from their house... and those who are good to whoever has hated them with words)

That is: they hated (qalaynā).

And His saying: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life]﴾. He means: the reward of Allah is better for you than the pleasures of this world.

It is related that ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon the Prophet and found him lying on a mat (ḥaṣīr), and the mat had left its mark on his side. ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) wept, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What makes you weep, ʿUmar?" He said: "I remembered Kisrā and Caesar and the pleasures they are in, while you are the Messenger of Allah [in this state]."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Are you not content that they should have the world, [and we have the Hereafter]?"

And His saying: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well-pleased﴾. That is: of reward, honour and station, until you are pleased. And in some of the exegeses it is said: it is a thousand palaces of pearls, and its dust is musk. The third opinion: it is the intercession (shafa'ah) for his community. And it is reported from Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir, who said: "You say that the most hopeful verse in the Book of God the Exalted is His saying: ﴿Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God﴾ [39:53], and the verse... And we say: the most hopeful verse in the Book of God the Exalted is His saying: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well-pleased﴾." He means: that He will grant him intercession for his community until he is pleased.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 93, verse 6:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?﴾ He named him an orphan because his father died while he was still in the womb. It is also said: two months after his birth. His mother died when he was six years old, and his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muttalib took charge of him (kafala). Then the grandfather died when he was eight years old, and his paternal uncle Abu Ṭalib took charge of him. The meaning of His words ﴿and give you shelter﴾ is: He made for you a refuge (maʾwa), and that was Abu Ṭalib. The meaning is: you took refuge in him. Abu Ṭalib died three years before the Hijra.

And His saying: ﴿And He found you lost, and guided you﴾. That is: lost from the sacred laws and Islam, and He guided you to them. It is also said: lost from prophethood. It was said: "lost" means heedless of what was intended for you, and He guided you to it, and this is the best of the opinions.

It was also said: "lost" from the path of truth, and He guided you to it.

And it is reported from some of them: He found you among a people who were astray. The most preferable of the opinions is that it be understood in terms of the sacred laws, and what God revealed, like His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾. Or the meaning may be: He found you "lost," that is, heedless of prophethood and the revelation that was sent down to you, like His saying in the story of Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿He said: I did it then, when I was of those who were astray﴾, that is, of the heedless.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 93, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿And He found you poor, and enriched you﴾. That is: destitute, and He enriched you with the wealth of Khadija.

[Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said]: He enriched you with contentment and satisfaction with what He gave you, and this is the better of the two opinions. It is also established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Richness is not from abundance of goods; true richness is richness of the heart." And some of them recited:

(The poor man does not know when he will become rich, and the rich man does not know when he will become poor.)

That is: he will become poor (yaftaqir).

It is also said: ﴿And He found you dependent⁠⁠ﾠ﻿⁠ﾠ[...]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾. That is, do not belittle him. And "qahr" (oppression) means: do not wrong him, that is, take his right and strengthen yourself through it. The people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) used to do this with the wealth of orphans.

Ibn Mas'ud recited: "fa-la takhar" (فَلَا تَكْهَر), meaning: do not rebuke him harshly.

And as for the one who asks, do not repel him harshly. That is, turn him away gently and softly: either give to him, or decline him gently and pray for him. It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: it is meant concerning the seeker of knowledge, not the seeker of food. And it is related from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, that whenever a seeker of knowledge came to him he would say: "Welcome to the beloved ones of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." And it is related from Ibrahim ibn Adham, may Allah sanctify his soul, that he said: "I think that Allah, the Exalted, averts punishment from the people of the world because of the journeys of the people of hadith in seeking knowledge."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 93, verse 11:

And the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And as for the favour of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, i.e., by prophethood.

And His saying: ﴿proclaim it﴾, i.e., call the people to it. He had concealed it for a time and then made it manifest. It was also said: it is the Qur'an, and according to this His saying ﴿proclaim it﴾ means: recite it to the people. And it is said: it refers to all blessings.

And His saying: ﴿proclaim it﴾, i.e., make it manifest through thankfulness. And it is related from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "When you obtain some good or a blessing, then report it to the trustworthy among your brothers."

And it is related from 'Amr ibn Maymun that he said: "Whoever stands in prayer at night for his portion, there is no harm in his telling of it to a trustworthy one among his brothers, saying: 'Allah has provided me with such and such.'"

And in some reports: "Making a blessing manifest is thankfulness, and remaining silent about it is ingratitude." And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, recited with takbir from this place to the end of the Qur'an at the end of each surah. He mentioned that he recited to Mujahid, and Mujahid instructed him to do so. Mujahid recited to Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and he instructed him to do so. Ibn 'Abbas recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with them both, and he instructed him to do so. Ibn Mas'ud recited to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he instructed him to do so.

The takbir is the saying: Allahu Akbar. They said: The reason for this is that when the polytheists said to the Prophet (ﷺ), "Your Lord has abandoned you and become displeased with you," and in another report they said, "His devil has forsaken him," then when Allah the Exalted sent down this surah, in which is His saying ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He become displeased﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) gave takbir out of joy at the revelation of this surah, and it became a sunnah until the end of the Qur'an.

And Allah knows best.
